install_symbols.why: zECS's install jobs (JCL/CONFIG.jcl, DEFEXPR.jcl) replace @ecs_hlq@ and @environment@ in ZCEXPIRE.idcams and the CSD's DEFINE FILE(ZCEXPIRE) DSNAME; this case installs one environment, high-level qualifier ZECS and environment TEST; #5089: the instance (ID 01) the resume scenarios name through their start data, so the CSD's ZC@ID@FILE and ZC@ID@KEY are ZC01FILE and ZC01KEY (EIBTRNID / ZC-TRANID 'ZC01')

vsam.why: Source/ZCEXPIRE.idcams: INDEXED KEYS(4 0) RECORDSIZE(80 2048), RECORDFORMAT(V) in the CSD. Every record the program writes and reads is its ZX-RECORD, 70 bytes (LENGTH OF ZX-RECORD), whose first 4 bytes are the key

Source/ZECSFILE.idcams: INDEXED KEYS(16 0) RECORDSIZE(100 32700); the CSD's DEFINE FILE(ZC@ID@FILE) DSNAME is @ECS_HLQ@.ZC@ID@FILE.@ENVIRONMENT@ and the engine does not read the IDCAMS job as a define. The CSD defines it RECORDFORMAT(V); every record the case seeds is the one length reclen (a seed line is a ZF record, ZF-KEY-16 .. ZF-DATA as written, which the harness blank-pads to the program's ZF-RECORD of 32700 bytes), so the stub's fixed-length records stand in

Source/ZECSKEY.idcams: INDEXED KEYS(255 0) RECORDSIZE(512 512); the CSD's DEFINE FILE(ZC@ID@KEY) DSNAME is @ECS_HLQ@.ZC@ID@KEY.@ENVIRONMENT@, not read as a define (RECORDFORMAT(V) there, fixed 512-byte records in the stub)

scenarios.name: interval-not-elapsed
scenarios.why: the control record ZX01 on file was written 600 s before the task (its interval is 1800 s): 1400-UPDATE finds RELATIVE-TIME below the TTL, so 8000-RESTART (START TRANSID(EIBTRNID) INTERVAL(1500) with the 20-byte ZC-PARM) and 9000-RETURN end the task before the expiration browse of the instance's file

scenarios.name: control-record-duprec

faults.why: the control record is not on file: 1300-WRITE
another expiration task wrote it first

scenarios.why: READ UPDATE of the control record NOTFND, so 1300-WRITE writes it, and the WRITE answers DUPREC (a task of the same instance wrote it first): 8000-RESTART and 9000-RETURN end the task before the browse

scenarios.name: enq-busy

faults.why: another expiration task of the instance holds the ENQ (NOSUSPEND: the task is not suspended, ENQBUSY is raised)

scenarios.why: 1200-ENQ ENQ RESOURCE(ZC-EXPIRE-ENQ) NOSUSPEND answers ENQBUSY (IBM raises it for an unavailable resource with NOSUSPEND; register X60): 8000-RESTART and 9000-RETURN end the task before the control record is read

scenarios.name: resume-empty-file
scenarios.why: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM: ZC-TRANID ZC01, ZC-KEY not LOW-VALUES), so 1100-CONTROL is skipped and the instance's file names resolve at run time (#4771, #5089): ZF-FCT = ZC01FILE, ZK-FCT = ZC01KEY, both the one ZC##FILE / ZC##KEY store stated by this case's datasets. ZC01FILE is empty: 2000-READ-FILE's READ GTEQ answers NOTFND, so EOF is set and 8000-RESTART and 9000-RETURN end the task

scenarios.name: resume-fresh-record
scenarios.why: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM: ZC-TRANID ZC01, ZC-KEY not LOW-VALUES), so 1100-CONTROL is skipped and the instance's file names resolve at run time (#4771, #5089): ZF-FCT = ZC01FILE, ZK-FCT = ZC01KEY, both the one ZC##FILE / ZC##KEY store stated by this case's datasets. the READ GTEQ finds FRESH1 (ZF-ABS an hour ahead of the clock): it has not expired, so 3000-DEPLICATE (DOCUMENT / WEB) is not run and the record is kept; the next READ GTEQ is NOTFND and the task restarts and returns

scenarios.name: resume-expired-peer-201
scenarios.why: #5089: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM), so 1100-CONTROL is skipped and ZF-FCT / ZK-FCT resolve to ZC01FILE / ZC01KEY (#4771, #5089). The first record, EXPRD1 (two segments), has ZF-ABS an hour and a minute before the clock and a ZF-TTL of 3600 s, so RELATIVE-TIME exceeds TTL-MILLISECONDS and 3000-DEPLICATE runs: the active-standby partner answers 201 with its own ABSTIME in the status text (numeric), so 3100-UPDATE-ABS READs the record for update and 3110-REWRITE stores the partner's ABSTIME in ZF-ABS and SYNCPOINTs: the record is kept, not deleted. FRESH1 is kept and the next READ GTEQ is NOTFND

scenarios.name: resume-expired-peer-404
scenarios.why: #5089: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM), so 1100-CONTROL is skipped and ZF-FCT / ZK-FCT resolve to ZC01FILE / ZC01KEY (#4771, #5089). The first record, EXPRD1 (two segments), has ZF-ABS an hour and a minute before the clock and a ZF-TTL of 3600 s, so RELATIVE-TIME exceeds TTL-MILLISECONDS and 3000-DEPLICATE runs: the partner answers 404 (status text not numeric), so 3200-DELETE runs: 3210-DELETE issues DELETE FILE(ZF-FCT) once per segment (ZF-SEGMENT 1 to ZF-SEGMENTS) and DELETE FILE(ZK-FCT) removes the key record; both files are the run-time ZC01FILE / ZC01KEY stores

scenarios.name: resume-expired-single
scenarios.why: #5089: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM), so 1100-CONTROL is skipped and ZF-FCT / ZK-FCT resolve to ZC01FILE / ZC01KEY (#4771, #5089). The first record, EXPRD1 (two segments), has ZF-ABS an hour and a minute before the clock and a ZF-TTL of 3600 s, so RELATIVE-TIME exceeds TTL-MILLISECONDS and 3000-DEPLICATE runs: the document template ZC01DC is not defined, so DOCUMENT CREATE is not NORMAL, 7000-GET-URL sets DC-TYPE to A1 (single data center) and no WEB OPEN / CONVERSE / CLOSE is issued; with EIBRESP not NORMAL and not LENGERR the record is neither rewritten nor deleted and the browse goes on

scenarios.name: control-record-first-write
scenarios.why: #6072: the ZCEXPIRE file holds no control record for ZX01 (an empty seed), so 1100-CONTROL's READ UPDATE answers NOTFND and 1300-WRITE writes the record; the WRITE succeeds (no DUPREC, line 354 false), 1300-EXIT and 1100-EXIT are reached and the task goes on to the expiration browse of the instance's (empty) file

scenarios.name: interval-elapsed
scenarios.why: #6072: the control record ZX01 was written 3000 s before the task (clock 10:30:15; its interval is 1800 s): 1400-UPDATE finds RELATIVE-TIME not below the TTL (line 381 false), REWRITEs the record with the new ABSTIME, and 1400-EXIT and 1100-EXIT are reached before the expiration browse of the instance's file

scenarios.name: expired-single-dc-delete
scenarios.why: #6072: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM), so ZF-FCT / ZK-FCT resolve to ZC01FILE / ZC01KEY (#4771, #5089). The document template ZC01DC holds only 'type: A1' (DC-LENGTH under TEN): DOCUMENT CREATE and RETRIEVE are NORMAL, so 7000-GET-URL leaves EIBRESP NORMAL and sets DC-TYPE to A1 (single data center). In 3000-DEPLICATE the three IFs on EIBRESP NORMAL are therefore true while DC-TYPE is neither AA nor AS (lines 446, 451, 457 false arm): no WEB OPEN / CONVERSE / CLOSE is issued, WEB-STATUS-CODE is not 201, and 3200-DELETE removes the expired record's segments and its key record

scenarios.name: expired-12-delete
scenarios.why: #6072: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM), so ZF-FCT / ZK-FCT resolve to ZC01FILE / ZC01KEY (#4771, #5089). 12 expired records (E00001..E00012, two segments each, the same key path) and a single-data-center template: every record goes through 3200-DELETE. RECORD-COUNT passes TEN on the 11th delete and 3220-SYNCPOINT runs (line 531 true arm: RECORD-COUNT back to zero, SYNCPOINT, DELAY INTERVAL(0)); DELETE-COUNT stays far under FIVE-HUNDRED (line 535 true arm is not reached here: see the case notes)

scenarios.name: expired-peer-https
scenarios.why: #6072: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM), so ZF-FCT / ZK-FCT resolve to ZC01FILE / ZC01KEY (#4771, #5089). The partner is named by an https URL in the template: 7000-GET-URL's WEB PARSE answers SCHEMENAME HTTPS, so 7100-WEB-OPEN takes the HTTPS arm (line 620 true) and moves DFHVALUE(HTTPS) to URL-SCHEME; the partner answers 404 and the expired record is deleted

scenarios.name: expired-peer-201-update-fails
scenarios.why: #6072: the task is started with start data (RETRIEVE INTO ZC-PARM), so ZF-FCT / ZK-FCT resolve to ZC01FILE / ZC01KEY (#4771, #5089). The partner answers 201 with a numeric ABSTIME, so 3100-UPDATE-ABS issues READ FILE(ZC01FILE) UPDATE, the second READ on that file after the browse READ GTEQ; the fault makes it answer NOTFND, so the IF on EIBRESP NORMAL (line 486) takes its false arm and 3110-REWRITE is skipped: the record keeps its old ABSTIME and the browse goes on

faults.why: the READ UPDATE of the record just browsed answers NOTFND (a concurrent delete by the other region's expiration task)

scenarios.name: expired-501-delete
scenarios.why: #6072: 501 expired records (E00001..E00501, two segments each, the same key path) and a single-data-center template (type: A1): every record goes through 3200-DELETE. DELETE-COUNT passes FIVE-HUNDRED on the 501st delete (line 535 true), so 8100-RESTART (START TRANSID INTERVAL(2) with the 20-byte ZC-PARM) and 9000-RETURN end the task with the browse unfinished; RECORD-COUNT passes TEN every 11th delete and 3220-SYNCPOINT runs 45 times

scenarios.name: expired-501-peer-201
scenarios.why: #6072: 501 expired records (E00001..E00501, two segments each) and an active-standby template (type: AS) whose partner answers every DELETE 201 with a numeric ABSTIME: each record goes through 3100-UPDATE-ABS and 3110-REWRITE keeps it with the partner's ABSTIME. RESET-COUNT passes FIVE-HUNDRED on the 501st rewrite (line 508 true), so 8100-RESTART (START TRANSID INTERVAL with the 20-byte ZC-PARM) and 9000-RETURN end the task with the browse unfinished; 501 WEB OPEN / CONVERSE / CLOSE rounds, past the stub's former 64-session and 256-response caps (#6777)

notes: zECS's expiration task for one instance (ZECS000, started by the ZX## transaction, here ZX01: EIBTRNID names the instance's files ZC01FILE and ZC01KEY, and the control file ZCEXPIRE). #5089: the CICS file ZCEXPIRE is defined with install symbols (CSD DEFINE FILE DSNAME @ecs_hlq@.ZCEXPIRE.@environment@) and zECS's IDCAMS job is Source/ZCEXPIRE.idcams, which the engine does not read as a define. The case states the substitution ("install_symbols": ECS_HLQ ZECS, ENVIRONMENT TEST -- never guessed) and the file's KEYS(4 0) from that job ("vsam" under the resolved name). RECORDSIZE(80 2048) and RECORDFORMAT(V) make ZCEXPIRE a variable-length KSDS; the stub keeps fixed-length records, so the case states reclen 70 -- every record the program writes and reads is its ZX-RECORD (LENGTH OF ZX-RECORD) -- and "variable": true says so; a record of another length would be a different case. The control record in zcexpire.bin is the one written 600 s before the task. The task is started with no start data (RETRIEVE answers ENDDATA: ZC-KEY stays LOW-VALUES) at the harness's STARTCODE 'S'. HOLES, named: ZC##FILE and ZC##KEY are named at run time from the RETRIEVEd transaction id (#4771) and defined by zECS's own IDCAMS jobs with install placeholders, so the Java side refuses the READ of the instance's file by name (Hole 'CICS file FILE: no store in the generated project') where GnuCOBOL answers FILENOTFOUND; every path that goes on to the expiration browse (2000-READ-FILE and everything after: the DOCUMENT / WEB replication, 3100-3220 deletes, 8100-RESTART) is therefore not in the case, and its paragraphs are uncovered and unproven (coverage 9/38 paragraphs). The two scenarios end before it: the control record is too young (1400-UPDATE restarts and returns) and a WRITE of the control record that answers DUPREC (1300-WRITE). ENQ BUSY, the control file's other conditions are not reached; the HANDLE ABEND label 9100-ABEND is reached by an AFCR / AFCS / AFCT abend planned on the control READ (#6271, X70) (the harness plans no fault for ENQ). Derived from zECS (github.com/walmartlabs/zECS, Apache-2.0): LICENSE here is the corpus's own, NOTICE names the source and what was derived. #5089 (#4771): two scenarios start the task with start data naming the instance (ZC01), so ZC##FILE / ZC##KEY resolve to the stated datasets ZECS.ZC01FILE.TEST / ZECS.ZC01KEY.TEST (the same stores and seeds as zecs-zecs003) and 2000-READ-FILE runs. The expired-record path (3000-DEPLICATE: DOCUMENT / WEB replication, the 3100-3220 deletes) is still not in the case.
compiler_options_why: #5089: the program MOVEs LENGTH OF ZF-RECORD (32700) to ZF-LENGTH, a PIC S9(04) COMP, then READs LENGTH(ZF-LENGTH): TRUNC(STD) stores 2700 there and every full-size record would be LENGERR (a record over 2700 bytes could never be read), so the program only works as shipped under TRUNC(BIN); ASMZECS.jcl's DFHYITVL step states no TRUNC option (assumption, register it)
